advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the added per-write `git rev-parse` in `_ensure_initialized` is acceptable on the write hot path (or cache/skip it when `.git` is present).
evidence: Old guard: `if not os.path.isdir(tracker) or not os.path.exists(os.path.join(tracker, ".git")):` — no subprocess
New guard: `if not store_is_usable(tracker):` which calls `_head_resolves` → `run_git_bounded(tracker, "rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", "HEAD", ...)` (store_usability.py:106)
event_append.py:124/160/309/332 each call `_ensure_initialized(tracker)` on the write path
store_usability.py:145: `.git` present + resolvable HEAD is the FIRST clause, so the git subprocess runs for every normal live store
advisory.finding: _ensure_initialized now spawns a git rev-parse subprocess on every write op, where it was previously a pure-filesystem check (os.path.isdir + os.path.exists). It is invoked at each event_append write entry point (stage_and_commit, batch_stage_and_commit, batch_stage_and_commit_under_lock, delete_events) and adds a fork/exec+git-startup cost to the common case (a live store with a resolvable HEAD), with no caching of the result.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile store_is_usable's fall-through behavior with the docstring claim that a mid-clone (`.git` present, HEAD unresolvable) store is always rejected — either short-circuit on `.git` present + unresolvable HEAD, or soften the docstrings.
evidence: store_usability.py:145-147: `if os.path.exists(os.path.join(tracker, ".git")) and _head_resolves(tracker): return True` then `return _carries_store_structure(tracker)` — unresolvable HEAD does NOT short-circuit to False
event_prepare.py docstring: 'a mid-clone store (no HEAD, no structure) is still rejected' and 'The predicate's .git-less STRUCTURE clause ... cannot loosen this write gate in practice'
store_usability.py:29-31 claims only a store with 'no .git, no committed record, no ticket dirs' fails both clauses — a `.git`+unresolvable-HEAD store WITH structure is not covered by that claim
advisory.finding: The docstrings assert a mid-clone store (`.git` present, HEAD unresolvable) is 'still rejected' and that the write gate 'does not loosen in practice', but store_is_usable falls through to _carries_store_structure whenever HEAD does not resolve. A store with an unresolvable HEAD that already has a checked-out ticket event dir or a `.store-compat.json` on disk would be reported USABLE, contradicting the stated mid-clone rejection guarantee.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether _carries_store_structure's event-dir fallback should require the subdirectory to actually contain a ticket event file rather than accepting any non-dot subdir.
evidence: store_usability.py:127-130: `return any(not entry.startswith(".") and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(tracker, entry)) for entry in entries)` — no check that the subdir actually contains a ticket event (e.g. a NNN-*.json)

Docstring at store_usability.py:118 asserts 'A genuinely broken store (marker FILES only, no committed record, no ticket dirs) carries neither and is not usable' — but a broken store with any stray subdir would pass
advisory.finding: _carries_store_structure's event-dir fallback accepts ANY non-dot subdirectory as evidence of store structure, not only a well-formed ticket event directory. A `.git`-less directory that happens to contain a single unrelated subdirectory is therefore judged a usable store rather than an uninitialized/broken one.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid spawning a `git rev-parse` subprocess per read: cache/memoize the `store_is_usable` HEAD-probe result per tracker within a read context (or gate the audit index loop behind a single usability check + `local_read_context`) so git-subprocess count does not scale with ticket count.
evidence: `store_usability.py:106` `result = run_git_bounded(tracker, "rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", "HEAD", timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT)` — an unconditional subprocess spawn on the common `.git`-present path
`store_usability.py:145` `if os.path.exists(os.path.join(tracker, ".git")) and _head_resolves(tracker):` — the HEAD probe runs for every usable live store, not just once
`_reads.py:57` `if not store_is_usable(tracker):` — every read entry point (`_reads.py:116,140,188,199,210,230,247`) calls `_tracker` -> `store_is_usable` with no caching/memoization
audit/server.py:114-119 `for ticket in tickets: ... trail = audit_trail(tid, repo_root=repo_root)` — pre-existing per-ticket loop
audit/read.py:205-217 `audit_trail` fans out into `rebar_show`, `list_tickets(ticket_type="code_review")`, nested `show_ticket` per candidate, and sidecar reads — each funneling through `_tracker`

ABSENCE: `store_is_usable` performs no per-request caching/memoization of the HEAD-probe result, so the subprocess runs once per read call, i.e. O(number-of-reads) which scales with ticket count on the audit index
advisory.finding: The new `store_is_usable` predicate spawns a `git rev-parse HEAD` subprocess on every `_reads._tracker` call, and `_tracker` is invoked per-read on the audit index's per-ticket fan-out loop, so the number of git child processes scales with the ticket count (an amplified N+1) on each audit index render.
scenarios: Audit web index (`_audited_tickets`) rendered against a store with a large, user-controlled number of tickets: git subprocess spawns scale with ticket count times per-ticket read fan-out
Any batch/loop caller that issues many library/MCP reads against one live store within a single logical operation
advisory.suggested_fix: Cache the store-usability verdict per tracker path for the duration of a read context (e.g. compute once in `_audited_tickets`/`local_read_context` and reuse), or short-circuit `store_is_usable` inside an active pinned/read view where the tracker was already validated, so the HEAD probe runs at most once per logical read operation rather than once per read call.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the stale `_ensure_initialized requires tracker/.git` note in tests/unit/test_store_copy_needs_env_id.py:12 with the widened predicate, or confirm/document that a `.git`-less-but-structured tracker passing the write gate is intended.
evidence: Old gate (diff): `if not os.path.isdir(tracker) or not os.path.exists(os.path.join(tracker, '.git')):`

New gate: src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py:114 `if not store_is_usable(tracker):` — store_is_usable returns True for a `.git`-less tracker via `_carries_store_structure` (store_usability.py: committed record OR any non-dot dir)
tests/unit/test_store_copy_needs_env_id.py:12 documents `_ensure_initialized requires tracker/.git` — that contract statement is now inaccurate
advisory.finding: The write gate `event_prepare._ensure_initialized` is loosened: it previously rejected any tracker lacking `.git` (`not os.path.exists(os.path.join(tracker, '.git'))`) but now accepts a `.git`-less tracker that merely 'carries store structure' (a `.store-compat.json` file OR any non-dot subdirectory). The documented contract in test_store_copy_needs_env_id.py:12 ('`event_append._ensure_initialized` requires `tracker/.git`') is now stale.
scenarios: A `.git`-less tracker that happens to carry a ticket event dir or a `.store-compat.json` now passes the write gate where it previously raised
The stale doc comment could mislead a future maintainer reasoning about the write gate's precondition

evidence: src/rebar/_reads.py:57 `if not store_is_usable(tracker):` replacing the old `if not os.path.isdir(tracker):` — a present-but-unusable dir now raises instead of reading `[]`
